chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sayf ibn ʿAmirah, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

I asked Aba ʿAbdillah عليه السلام about an owned slave who falsely accuses a free man. He said: “He is flogged eighty lashes. This is from the rights of the Muslims. But as for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he is struck with half of the hadd.” I said: What is that which is from the rights of Allah? He said: “If he commits zina or drinks wine, then this is from the rights in which half of the hadd is administered.”

key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: the rights regarded as belonging to Allah in legal classification
key_terms.حُقُوقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the rights belonging to people among the Muslims
key_terms.عَبْدٍ مَمْلُوكٍ: an owned slave under legal bondage
key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused someone of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.نِصْفَ الْحَدِّ: half of the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a slave who commits qadhf, zina, or drinks wine according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between offenses involving the rights of people and those involving the rights of Allah in the legal treatment of a slave. False accusation against a free Muslim incurs the full hadd of eighty lashes, while offenses such as zina and drinking wine are treated as rights of Allah for which a slave receives half the hadd. The narration is significant in fiqh for classifying legal penalties according to the nature of the violated right.
